data.turoyo: Məlle lu ḥmoro: "Zox payadlan šamʕo d maqəṯina bahro."
data.translation: Der Possenreisser sagte zum Esel: "Geh, hole uns doch eine Kerze, damit wir ein Licht anzünden".

rationale: Second Imperativ example under the sole inherited sense 1; candle object, beneficiary -lan and purpose clause are explicit.

summary: All four occurrences fit II.1 procurement; no new sense, form box or idiom. Two supplied passages repeat existing examples despite different citation formats. Null example sense labels in the source belong to the sole sense 1; inherited text is preserved.

Beneficiary -lan in payadlan contrasts with -la/-a in the existing examples. The prefixless Imperativ is already part of the entry, so payəd is not a new box. Permitted lookup confirms fyd II has the same etymology and gloss with f- forms; do not infer a regional distribution from these few tokens.

Align PrS 68/55 with inherited prs 194/27 and PrS 68/56 with inherited prs 103/140. Are these parallel text/page citation systems or an inherited miscitation? No fix-citation is justified by the present input alone.

PrS 84/56: what is the antecedent of implicit plural procurement object? The reader supplies goats, but this verse alone does not name them. Confirm p/f variation and geographic distribution from fuller source evidence.
